solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One who might have left in two different ways

definitions.text: One who might have left in two different ways

parts.words: One who might have left in two different ways
parts.note: the person making a will leaves property to heirs, and by the time it takes effect has also left this life

explanation.surface: A puzzle about someone whose departure can be read two ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' means both bequeathed and departed: a will-maker leaves goods and, by the time they pass on, has died.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the maker of a will both bequeaths property and has departed when it is read.

clue.text: Better money for authority

parts.note: top as a verb means better, surpass
brass is northern English slang for money

explanation.surface: Better pay for those in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Brass is northern English slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Collective term: the highest-ranking officers or officials are those in command.

clue.text: Bad mood? Drinks to be served up

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: ports are fortified wines

explanation.surface: Someone in a bad mood orders drinks to be served.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British word for a sulk or fit of temper.

clue.text: Work inspired by Venus de Milo?

definitions.text: Work inspired by Venus de Milo?

parts.words: Work inspired by Venus de Milo?
parts.note: the famous statue is missing its upper limbs, so a book title about parting from limbs fits it

explanation.surface: A question about art inspired by a famous Greek statue.
explanation.walkthrough: The Venus de Milo has lost both arms; Hemingway's novel title reads as a goodbye to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemingway's First World War novel, punningly fitted to an armless statue.

clue.text: Where man must go for executives, the asses

indicators.note: must go says the word man is removed and replaced

parts.note: managers are executives
taken as written
on answers where, as in placed on something

explanation.surface: Where managers must go, the asses — a dig at bosses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word: in MANAGERS the MAN 'must go' and ON takes its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the wild asses of central Asia are one species of donkey.

clue.text: Decline seconds, not ready?

parts.note: something unset, like jelly or concrete, is not yet ready

explanation.surface: Someone declines to wait a few seconds because they are not ready.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative synonym: the twilight of a career or empire is its period of decline.

clue.text: Short of hairpiece, yanked off and nicked?

parts.note: under means short of, less than
a lock is a piece of hair

indicators.note: off means the letters have gone wrong and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wig yanked off by a thief who is then arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals the anagram of YANKED to ANDKEY; 'nicked' is British slang for arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: secured in jail, as a person arrested or caught would be.

clue.text: Son left with runny guts having scoffed friend's cake

indicators.note: scoffed means eaten, so the pair takes in the friend

parts.note: an ally is a friend

indicators.note: guts means the inside letters of the word

explanation.surface: A boy with an upset stomach after eating a friend's cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having scoffed' means the son-and-left pair swallow the friend; 'guts' means the inside of runny. The cake is a Bath speciality.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a light sweet teacake from Bath, named after a legendary baker.

clue.text: Travel at leisure: device saving time and energy

indicators.note: saving here means keeping one letter inside the device

parts.note: a tool is a device
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A time and energy saving gadget for leisurely travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving' holds T inside TOOL, and E follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to potter along unhurriedly.

clue.text: Scream at Oliver, hiding explosive substance

indicators.note: hiding says the letters lie concealed in the words before it

explanation.surface: Someone shouts at Oliver, who is concealing explosives.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a high explosive made from TNT and ammonium nitrate.

clue.text: Quietly, otter sheds its first coat

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

indicators.note: the otter's name loses its opening letter

parts.note: Tarka the Otter is the hero of Henry Williamson's novel

explanation.surface: An otter quietly moults its outer coat.
explanation.walkthrough: The otter is Tarka, from Henry Williamson's classic English novel Tarka the Otter; 'sheds its first' drops the T, leaving ARKA.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a hooded windproof jacket is a kind of coat.

clue.text: Animal disturbed gorilla (not good) eating bananas

indicators.note: eating places one part inside another, as food goes inside the eater
disturbed letters are jumbled into a new order
not tells us to drop the letter for good from the ape's name

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy, mad

explanation.surface: An animal is upset when a gorilla eats bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not good' drops the G, 'disturbed' rearranges the rest into ARILLO, and 'eating' wraps that round the slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the armour-plated burrowing mammal of the Americas is an animal.

clue.text: Stand for now by religious teaching

parts.note: RE is religious education in British schools
the present is now

explanation.surface: A school declares its current position on religious education.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (religious education) is a British school subject; the charade runs in answer order, though 'now' comes first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to symbolise or speak on behalf of something is to stand for it.

clue.text: Sail this before we commission standard navy marines

definitions.meaning: a small sail set high on the mast above the topgallant

definitions.text: this before we commission standard navy marines
definitions.meaning: the same word precedes each of we, commission, standard, navy and marines to make familiar British phrases

explanation.surface: A naval officer lists what to commission before setting sail.
explanation.walkthrough: The royal we, a Royal Commission, the Royal Standard (the monarch's flag), the Royal Navy and the Royal Marines.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical term: the small square sail above the topgallant on a square-rigger.

clue.text: You left deliveries outside, on top of step

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means the first piece is followed by what comes after it
top of takes the first letter of the following word
the overs sit outside, around, the letter for left

parts.note: overs are sets of six deliveries in cricket

explanation.surface: Someone left parcels outside on the doorstep.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls bowled, so deliveries are OVERS; 'outside' wraps them round L.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword convention: the setter addresses the reader, who is a person tackling the puzzle.

clue.text: Help Handel and Brahms and Liszt

indicators.note: rhyming slang for drunk, so the letters are reeling

explanation.surface: Three composers apparently team up to help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brahms and Liszt' is Cockney rhyming slang for pissed, drunk: a drunken arrangement of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to assist or pitch in.

clue.text: Improve visit

definitions.meaning: to get better, as prospects do
to call on someone, as an old friend

explanation.definitionFit: Two phrasal-verb senses: things get better, and one calls in on an acquaintance.

clue.text: Big star treading clumsily

indicators.note: clumsily means the letters are put awkwardly in a new order

explanation.surface: A celebrity treading clumsily on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomy: a large, cool, luminous star late in its life.

clue.text: As one born in Lancashire town to the west

indicators.note: in places the letter for born inside the town's name
in an across clue, heading west means reading right to left

parts.note: Colne is a town in east Lancashire

explanation.surface: Someone born in a Lancashire town feels at one with it.
explanation.walkthrough: COLNE, a Lancashire mill town in northern England, read 'to the west' gives ENLOC, and 'in' puts B inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed French phrase meaning all together, as a single unit.

clue.text: Stone an old king without gawping heartlessly

indicators.note: without here means outside, surrounding

parts.note: Old King Cole is the merry monarch of the nursery rhyme

indicators.note: heartlessly removes all but the end letters

explanation.surface: A stone-faced old king who does not stare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' in its old sense means outside: the nursery-rhyme king goes round the two end letters that 'heartlessly' leaves of gawping.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialect word for a cobblestone or rounded pebble.

clue.text: Reportedly read something into one with suspicion

indicators.note: reportedly says the words are heard rather than seen

parts.note: one is A and read something is scans, so A SCANS is what is said

explanation.surface: A rumour makes someone look on another with suspicion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' signals a sound-alike: A (one) and SCANS (reads something) together sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: looking at someone sidelong, with distrust or doubt.

clue.text: Little boy, a month old, showing a certain style

parts.note: Art is a short form of the boy's name Arthur
Dec is short for December

explanation.surface: A baby boy, a month old, already showing style.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the geometric decorative design movement of the 1920s and 30s.

clue.text: Nothing wanting in flamboyant ship

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the letter goes

parts.note: baroque means flamboyant and ornate
O is the round zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A showy vessel that lacks nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a sailing vessel with three or more masts.

clue.text: Sadly not allowed to complete doctor's mission

indicators.note: the word for sadly is stopped before its last letter

parts.note: alas is said sadly
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor's mission is sadly halted before it is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' looks like an adverb on the surface but gives ALAS; cut short it is ALA.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Texan fort was originally a Spanish mission church.

clue.text: He made press corporation go short, seizing billions

parts.note: corporation is old slang for a pot belly, a gut

indicators.note: seizing means the shortened word holds the letter for billions
short drops the final letter

parts.note: go means energy or drive

explanation.surface: A media corporation forced to cut back after seizing billions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' and 'press' suggest business news; corporation is a humorous word for a big belly. 'short' gives ENERG and 'seizing' puts B inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Gutenberg invented the movable-type printing press in fifteenth-century Mainz.

clue.text: Wear armour regularly, or slip

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the words

explanation.surface: Wear armour, or risk a fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a small mistake.

clue.text: Dance from court, cross-examined after both sides quit

parts.note: a quad is a quadrangle, a college court

indicators.note: both ends of the word are dropped

parts.note: grilled means questioned hard

explanation.surface: A defendant cross-examined in court before both legal sides quit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link word; 'court' and 'cross-examined' set a legal scene, but court is a college quadrangle.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the square dance for four couples fashionable in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Final blow — actors sacking a film-maker

parts.note: KO is a knockout, the blow that ends a boxing match

indicators.note: sacking means dismissing the letter a

parts.note: RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, which trains actors

explanation.surface: A director's final blow is sacking the actors.
explanation.walkthrough: RADA is the leading London drama school; 'sacking a' removes one A from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Korda was a Hungarian-born British producer and director of films.

clue.text: Goal remains — the shorter version

parts.note: an end is a goal or aim
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A footballer's goal remains in the shortened highlights.
explanation.walkthrough: Typographers distinguish a longer and a shorter dash; the shorter is named for the width of a letter N.
explanation.definitionFit: Typographic term: the dash between em and hyphen in length is the shorter of the two dashes.

clue.text: Scriptures worthily translated

indicators.note: translated means the letters are changed into another form

explanation.surface: Sacred texts rendered faithfully into another language.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: sacred writings, especially the Bible, taken as authoritative.
